Let me understand the rule. We need to create input grids where exactly one stripe (full row or full column of a single non-black color) is fully intact. Actually the verifier just returns the first full row/column color found (scanning rows first, then columns). So the output is the color of the first completely-uniform nonzero row, else first completely-uniform nonzero column.

Let me design a few demonstration pairs. Note the verifier finds the first full row first, then columns. So I need to be careful: if a column is intact but a row is also fully intact... Actually the rule says exactly one stripe is fully intact. But the verifier picks rows before columns. To be safe, construct grids where only one stripe is intact.

Let me design grids.

Example: vertical stripes and horizontal stripes. A full column stripe is a column where all cells are the same color. A full row stripe is a row where all cells are same color.

But wait: a row could be fully uniform accidentally if all columns crossing it are same color. Need care.

Let me design simple cases.

Case 1: Only a row is intact.
Grid 6x6. Put a column stripe of color 3 at column 1 (all rows col1 = 3). Put a row stripe of color 2 at row 2 (all cols row2 = 2). Intersection at (2,1): row stripe overwrites -> 2. So column 1 is not fully uniform (has 2 at row2). Row 2 is fully 2 -> intact. Other columns: column 0 all 0? row2 col0 = 2, so column0 has 2. Not uniform. Output 2.

Actually simplest: replicate the example style.

Case where column is intact: horizontal stripe interrupted by vertical stripe. Row stripe color 3, column stripe color 2 passing through. Row interrupted, column intact. Output 2.

But verifier scans rows first. If row stripe is interrupted (has column color at intersection), row is not uniform. Column intact found. Good.

However potential issue: other rows might become uniform. E.g., rows without intersection: if a row has only background and column color... a row containing column stripe col c = color2 at position c and 0 elsewhere -> not uniform (has 0s and 2). Unless grid width 1. So fine.

Let me construct grids with multiple stripes to make rule clear.

Let me make grid 7x7.

Design: columns stripes at col1 color 4, col3 color 5. rows stripes at row2 color 2, row4 color 2? Hmm.

Actually the rule: stripes are rows or columns. Intersections, one overwrites. Exactly one intact.

Let me just create several valid examples.

Example A (row intact):
Row stripe color 6, columns stripe color 1 and 3.

Grid 6 wide, 6 tall.
Column 2 = color 1 (all rows). Column 4 = color 3 (all rows).
Row 3 = color 6 (all cols), overwriting at (3,2) and (3,4).

Row1: 0 0 1 0 3 0

Row3: 6 6 6 6 6 6
Row4: 0 0 1 0 3 0
Row5: 0 0 1 0 3 0

Check: row3 fully 6 -> intact. columns 2 and 4 not uniform due to 6 at row3. Other columns: col0 = 0,0,0,6,0,0 not uniform. col1 same. col3 same. col5 same. Output 6. Good.

Example B (column intact):
Row stripes color 7 at row1 and row4, column color 9 at col3 passing through.

Wait if column 9 intact, rows interrupted. Row1: 0..7..0 with col3=9 -> not uniform. Good.
